review.summary: The fix correctly handles relative color syntax by detecting a leading `from` keyword and offsetting channel indices by 2. Test coverage is solid including uppercase FROM, nested origin colors, and both accept/reject cases for hue-first and hue-third functions. Logic is straightforward and low-risk. Main gaps are around defensive coding for edge cases and missing test coverage for `lch(from ...)` variant.

issues.description: No test for `lch(from ...)` despite lch being in HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS
issues.detail: The reject/accept tests cover `oklch(from ...)` for the third-arg case but not `lch(from ...)`. Since both go through the same code path, a single test for lch would document intent and prevent future regressions if HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS membership changes.

issues.description: Assumes args[1] is always the origin color when `from` is present
issues.detail: The offset of 2 unconditionally assumes args[1] is a valid origin color. Malformed CSS like `oklch(from l c h)` (missing origin) would shift indices incorrectly and possibly miss/misreport the hue. Worth a defensive check or comment that malformed input falls through to the parser.

issues.description: `0 + offset` and `2 + offset` are stylistically odd
issues.detail: Writing `args[0 + offset]` reads awkwardly when offset is 0 in the non-relative case. Prefer `args[offset]` and `args[offset + 2]` (or define HUE_FIRST_INDEX/HUE_THIRD_INDEX constants) for clarity. Cosmetic only.

issues.description: Nested origin functions may produce duplicate-warning paths worth verifying
issues.detail: The test `hsl(FROM lch(0 0 10) 0 s l)` produces warnings on both the outer hsl hue (col 33) and inner lch hue (col 29). Confirm the walker doesn't double-report when the inner function is itself a hue-relevant function; the test seems to verify this, but it's worth a code comment about traversal order.
